english.title: Wear naval / military uniform without permission in manner / circumstances as likely to that bring uniform into contempt
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person not serving in His Majesty's military forces wore

(A)_[a uniform]_
(B)_[dress having the appearance of a uniform]_
(C)_[dress bearing the regimental or other distinctive mark]_

of the military force, namely **(..SPECIFY MILITARY FORCE..), without his Majesty's permission, and in such a manner or under such circumstances as to be likely to bring contempt upon that uniform, namely **(..SPECIFY CIRCUMSTANCES..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3 of the Uniforms Act 1894.

english.notes: Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Summary: One month imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
